vol1:fig-activation-checkpointing.scope: Original five activation positions with saved checkpoints, deterministic forward replay, and last-use release; activation counts are not total memory.

vol4:fig-11-intersample-overshoot.scope: Original acceleration and velocity curves with normalized computed values, equal endpoint velocities, and instantaneous acceleration reversal; no finite jerk bound.

vol1:fig-im2col-diagram.scope: Exact source values: channels 1–9 and 10–18; two 2 × 2 kernels stack into weights 1–8. Valid stride-one lowering creates four rows of eight values. This version materializes the buffer; implicit GEMM need not.

vol4:fig-05-action-taps.name: original-v4-05-action-taps
vol4:fig-05-action-taps.scope: Original four-tap architecture. Declared normalized toy values illustrate a clamp and stall; logical causal order, not measured network timing.

vol4:fig-07-open-vs-closed-loop.name: original-v4-07-open-vs-closed-loop
vol4:fig-07-open-vs-closed-loop.scope: Original two-panel plot, exact fixed one-degree heading series and axes. vol4:fig-10-latch-force-budget.name: original-v4-10-latch-force-budget
vol4:fig-10-latch-force-budget.scope: Original linear-spring/rigid-arm force plot and exact chapter profile. Braked and unbraked curves are alternative trajectories on one time axis; qualification and uncertainty are outside this model. An amplified spring glyph shows compression tied to the exact plotted force.
vol4:fig-10-latch-force-budget.question: Why size the stop from force at brake onset?

vol4:fig-12-capture-to-onset.name: original-v4-12-capture-to-onset
vol4:fig-12-capture-to-onset.scope: Original timing/travel strip, exact canonical interval endpoints at the chosen aisle speed. Dispatch allocation is unqualified; constant-speed travel maps the pre-onset budget only. Base icon follows the original travel row; icon size is schematic.

vol4:fig-14-authority-handshake-fsm.name: original-v4-14-authority-handshake-fsm
vol4:fig-14-authority-handshake-fsm.scope: Original per-channel authority FSM. Ordered successful handover, manual lease loss, guarded reset, and an explicit protective-preemption alternative. Normalized blend progress is illustrative.

vol4:fig-03-request-local-prefill-decode.name: original-v4-03-request-local-prefill-decode
vol4:fig-03-request-local-prefill-decode.scope: Original request-local schematic. Three input tiles and two decode passes illustrate ownership; tile counts are schematic, not tensor sizes or timing.
vol4:fig-03-request-local-prefill-decode.question: When does a sampled token acquire KV state?

vol4:fig-05-compounding-error-flywheel.name: original-v4-05-compounding-error-flywheel
vol4:fig-05-compounding-error-flywheel.scope: Original learner/plant loop and one schematic takeover. The five-second lookback is retained; the curve is conceptual, not a measured error trace.
vol4:fig-05-compounding-error-flywheel.question: Which takeover data can become expert labels?

vol4:fig-08-rolling-shutter-rows.name: original-v4-08-rolling-shutter-rows
vol4:fig-08-rolling-shutter-rows.scope: Canonical navigation-camera plot and its RollingShutterSkew LEGO inputs. A cursor samples rows; playback duration does not represent acquisition time.
vol4:fig-08-rolling-shutter-rows.question: How does row timing differ from exposure blur?

vol4:fig-10-mug-lease-timeline.name: original-v4-10-mug-lease-timeline
vol4:fig-10-mug-lease-timeline.scope: Canonical mug error curves and IntentLeaseArchetypes LEGO values. Error growth is stipulated model arithmetic, not measured tracking performance.
vol4:fig-10-mug-lease-timeline.question: Can evidence expire while the host still computes?

vol4:fig-13-loaded-tick.name: original-v4-13-loaded-tick
vol4:fig-13-loaded-tick.scope: Canonical loaded-tick FIFO model, with all original rows and thresholds. Aggregate interleaving and one-channel cases retain their original assumptions. Playback duration is illustrative; each operation can be inspected regardless of its modeled duration.
vol4:fig-13-loaded-tick.question: Does fitting within a period establish the timing premise?

vol4:fig-15-hardware-fault-injection.name: original-v4-15-hardware-fault-injection
vol4:fig-15-hardware-fault-injection.scope: Canonical model F1 witness timelines and speed curves, not empirical trials. All times share the last valid renewal as reference.
vol4:fig-15-hardware-fault-injection.question: Can travel pass while reaction timing fails?

vol1:fig-allocator-live-cached-blocks.name: original-v1-allocator-live-cached-blocks
vol1:fig-allocator-live-cached-blocks.scope: Original fixed virtual-address pool, expressed in the same twelve illustrative units. No growth, compaction, remapping, or pending device consumers. Snapshot (c) is split into two causal actions.
vol1:fig-allocator-live-cached-blocks.question: Why can six free units fail a six-unit request?

vol1:fig-calibration-ranges.name: original-v1-calibration-ranges
vol1:fig-calibration-ranges.scope: Original signed INT8 endpoints; same inputs and declared affine rounding/clipping policy.
vol1:fig-calibration-ranges.question: How do range and zero-point change the stored value?

vol1:fig-data-selection-resnet-data-path.name: original-v1-data-selection-resnet-data-path
vol1:fig-data-selection-resnet-data-path.scope: Same four stages and source full-epoch reference. A four-record toy trace retains A and C. The materialized coreset exists before the epoch; its construction cost is outside this replay. The default stream alternative follows the figure caption: all A–D are read, decoded, and copied before B/D are rejected from accelerator training arithmetic. Earlier metadata filtering is a separate possible design. No wall-clock speedup is inferred.
vol1:fig-data-selection-resnet-data-path.question: Where does a discarded image stop costing work?

vol1:fig-grad-accumulation.name: original-v1-grad-accumulation
vol1:fig-grad-accumulation.scope: Same three micro-batches as the original. Equal-size micro-batches; each gradient is from a sum-reduced loss, so their sum gives the full-batch sum gradient. No parameter update between micro-batches. Saved-activation labels indicate schematic storage, not a complete memory budget.
vol1:fig-grad-accumulation.question: What survives between micro-batches?

vol1:fig-kv-cache-growth.name: original-v1-kv-cache-growth
vol1:fig-kv-cache-growth.scope: Canonical 70B-class GQA model, FP16 KV, INT4 weights and the original H100 budget. A uniform-context batch is used for clarity. Capacity excludes runtime workspace, as in the source. Markers use the original curves and axes; motion is illustrative, not latency.
vol1:fig-kv-cache-growth.question: How do active requests compete with context length?

vol1:fig-python-tax.name: original-v1-python-tax
vol1:fig-python-tax.scope: The original five-operation timeline and its canonical Ops dispatch/launch values. One-microsecond kernels and the fused efficiency are the chapter’s declared scenario, not measurements or general compilation gains. Eager and compiled/fused rows are alternatives; the source chart omits per-kernel driver-launch cost on the eager row.
vol1:fig-python-tax.question: What keeps the next kernel from starting?

vol1:fig-systolic-array.name: original-v1-systolic-array
vol1:fig-systolic-array.scope: Declared weight-stationary 2×2 slice inside the original schematic: row inputs 2 and 3, every PE weight 1, two-term column reductions. Horizontal values and vertical partial sums advance on explicit skewed clocks. Other source FIFOs/accumulators illustrate the surrounding array and are outside this slice. No full-array utilization or DRAM-saving model.
vol1:fig-systolic-array.question: How does a skewed wavefront reuse neighboring values?

vol1:fig-training-attention-storage.name: original-v1-training-attention-storage
vol1:fig-training-attention-storage.scope: Same two forward paths and memory boundary as the original. A declared one-query/four-key, two-block toy row (scores 0, 0, ln 2, ln 2; values 2, 4, 6, 8) keeps running row statistics and partial output; the original matrix boxes stand for the full intermediates of this row trace, not a quadratic-capacity measurement; all backward/optimizer memory is omitted. Tiled execution is a separate alternative to the materialized path.
vol1:fig-training-attention-storage.question: Which intermediates cross into HBM?

vol4:fig-02-motor-torque-speed-envelope.name: original-v4-02-motor-torque-speed-envelope
vol4:fig-02-motor-torque-speed-envelope.scope: The source motor voltage/duty envelope plus its illustrative installed first-order thermal model. The threefold-current burst stays below peak torque. Cold and hot curves are alternative initial histories, not successive bursts; model horizons are not certified operating permission.

vol4:fig-04-multirate-cadence-buffer.name: original-v4-04-multirate-cadence-buffer
vol4:fig-04-multirate-cadence-buffer.scope: Two source panels use different scales: mailbox events are ordered, not timed; the upper schedule uses the chapter's milliseconds. A/B payload cells are illustrative identities. The application processor sends frames into MCU-owned memory; no shared AP/MCU storage is implied.
vol4:fig-04-multirate-cadence-buffer.question: Why can an unchanged mailbox never renew a command lease?

vol4:fig-06-diffusion-denoising.name: original-v4-06-diffusion-denoising
vol4:fig-06-diffusion-denoising.scope: The original three-panel schematic. Curve morphs illustrate dependent refinement, not a trained sampler or measured execution time. ACT 40 ms and illustrative diffusion 48 ms are separate schedule comparisons; they do not measure these drawn stages.

vol4:fig-09-rack-end-erosion.name: original-v4-09-rack-end-erosion
vol4:fig-09-rack-end-erosion.scope: The hull stays fixed. The growing region is a conservative possible-person reach set, not an observed person or a predicted walking trajectory. Source clearances and walking-speed bound come from the chapter; playback is not real time.
vol4:fig-09-rack-end-erosion.question: What does an aging free-space claim still certify?

vol4:fig-13-thermal-hysteresis.name: original-v4-13-thermal-hysteresis
vol4:fig-13-thermal-hysteresis.scope: The chapter's stipulated first-order cooldown and fixed work budget, not a measured device trace. Cooling time is seconds; each inspected permission response is microseconds. No general safety or WCET proof is inferred.

vol4:fig-frame-staleness-error.name: original-v4-frame-staleness-error

vol1:fig-irregular-address-transactions.scope: Four-byte words, sixteen-byte aligned sectors; cold cache/no reuse/within-sector merging. Independent address-dependency example.

vol1:fig-neuron-to-machine.scope: Two examples, two inputs and outputs, active two-by-two corner of source four-by-four PE array; no bias or activation.

vol1:fig-tiling-diagram.scope: A selected 2 × 2 output tile reduces K = 6 through three K tiles of width 2. The source layout includes a resident accumulator inset.

vol3:fig-vol3-block-diagonal-mask.scope: Original two examples with five and three tokens. A declared toy row uses equal finite scores of zero; softmax is computed in JavaScript. No kernel speedup is implied.

vol3:fig-vol3-collection-pipeline.name: original-v3-collection-pipeline
vol3:fig-vol3-collection-pipeline.scope: One tracked run through the original four responsibilities; other in-flight credits remain unchanged. Motion is logical, not a rate model.

vol3:fig-vol3-hierarchical-budget.scope: Canonical dollar balances from the original figure. JavaScript uses integer mills to preserve the displayed budget; logical animation does not model billing time.
vol3:fig-vol3-hierarchical-budget.question: Why does stopping a child release no root funds?

vol3:fig-vol3-intent-before-dispatch.name: original-v3-intent-before-dispatch
vol3:fig-vol3-intent-before-dispatch.scope: Original event order and recovery bands. A marker follows one operation; it does not measure elapsed time.
vol3:fig-vol3-intent-before-dispatch.question: What does a durable intent establish after a crash?

vol3:fig-vol3-radix-tree-cache.name: original-v3-radix-tree-cache
vol3:fig-vol3-radix-tree-cache.scope: Original radix prefix tree and active request path. Four drawn block symbols per node are illustrative ownership objects, not a byte-capacity model.
vol3:fig-vol3-radix-tree-cache.question: Why must eviction proceed from dormant leaves?

vol3:fig-vol3-search-topologies.scope: Original illustrative topologies: four best-of-N candidates, beam width two, and one selected tree path. Counts describe this drawing; no quality or runtime advantage is implied.

vol3:fig-vol3-access-prefilter.scope: The original filtered graph and response sketches. A blue ring records an examined eligible node; it does not change permission. vol3:fig-vol3-checkpoint-consistent-cut.name: original-v3-checkpoint-consistent-cut

vol2:fig-checkpoint-recovery-timeline.scope: Original two-save schematic progress timeline, without physical time or progress units.

vol2:fig-continuous-batching-comparison.scope: Exact four-slot/eight-iteration source trace; occupancy is not latency, prefill and decode unequal.

vol2:fig-fusion-before-after.scope: Original HBM-boundary chain; symbolic intermediate tensors; intermediate traffic only.

vol2:fig-gpudirect-data-path.name: original-v2-gpudirect-data-path
vol2:fig-gpudirect-data-path.scope: The sending-node layout and paths from the original diagram. Compare two separate sends of the same symbolic n-byte payload; no time or throughput scale.
vol2:fig-gpudirect-data-path.question: Which copies disappear with GPUDirect RDMA?

vol2:fig-hierarchical-allreduce.name: original-v2-hierarchical-allreduce
vol2:fig-hierarchical-allreduce.scope: Original two-node/two-GPU hierarchy; provenance identifies contributors, no timing or byte model.
vol2:fig-hierarchical-allreduce.question: How do local partial sums become a full result on every GPU?

vol2:fig-inference-lifecycle.name: original-v2-inference-lifecycle
vol2:fig-inference-lifecycle.scope: Declared token identities: prompt p0,p1; sampled outputs y0,y1. One request crosses CPU/GPU. KV entries are created only for tokens actually consumed as model inputs.
vol2:fig-inference-lifecycle.question: When does a generated token enter the KV cache?

vol2:fig-moe-all-to-all-routing.name: original-v2-moe-all-to-all-routing
vol2:fig-moe-all-to-all-routing.scope: The original sixteen tokens a–p, four ranks, and one expert per rank. Top-1 routing; prime marks an expert output, not a numerical value. One forward pass; backward exchanges are outside this sequence.
vol2:fig-moe-all-to-all-routing.question: How does each expert result find its original token?

vol2:fig-paged-attention.name: original-v2-paged-attention
vol2:fig-paged-attention.scope: Source eight-block example; A/B reservation and C/D admission are different snapshots; block not token.
vol2:fig-paged-attention.question: How can free blocks admit E without a contiguous gap?

vol2:fig-performance-engineering-flashat.name: original-v2-performance-engineering-flashattention-tiling
vol2:fig-performance-engineering-flashat.scope: Declared scalar worked case for one query: score blocks [1],[3], value blocks [2],[6]. The original HBM ↔ registers/SRAM boundary is retained. Values are toy data, not the chapter’s model workload.
vol2:fig-performance-engineering-flashat.question: Why must online softmax rescale earlier tiles?

vol2:fig-pfc-credit-deadlock.name: original-v2-pfc-credit-deadlock
vol2:fig-pfc-credit-deadlock.scope: The original four-switch cycle, with four declared toy packet slots per queue. For this toy only, full queues pause their predecessor and any free slot allows resume. A watchdog drops one packet; real thresholds and recovery policies vary.
vol2:fig-pfc-credit-deadlock.question: What must change before a deadlocked queue can forward?

vol2:fig-pipeline-parallelism.name: original-v2-pipeline-parallelism
vol2:fig-pipeline-parallelism.scope: Original GPipe four-stage four-microbatch forward-then-backward trace; activation presence, no byte or measured-time model.
vol2:fig-pipeline-parallelism.question: What stays in memory while the pipeline fills and drains?

vol2:fig-responsible-ai-architecture.name: original-v2-responsible-ai-architecture
vol2:fig-responsible-ai-architecture.scope: Declared schematic decision D7, group G, prediction positive; delayed outcome negative. Event identities illustrate joins, not measured fairness or a production data policy.
vol2:fig-responsible-ai-architecture.question: How do delayed outcomes become valid monitoring evidence?

vol2:fig-shadow-deployment.name: original-v2-shadow-deployment
vol2:fig-shadow-deployment.scope: The original shadow and canary panels. Declared toy batch R0–R19. Shadow copies every input; the separate canary batch sends one of twenty requests to the candidate, matching the illustrated 5 percent stage. No latency or quality result is assumed.
vol2:fig-shadow-deployment.question: When can a candidate response reach a user?

vol2:fig-speculative-decoding.name: original-v2-speculative-decoding
vol2:fig-speculative-decoding.scope: Declared source outcome trace, exact-algorithm gates but no probability simulation or latency estimate.
vol2:fig-speculative-decoding.question: Which draft tokens actually become output?

vol2:fig-time-travel.name: original-v2-time-travel
vol2:fig-time-travel.scope: Original ten-click example. Each numbered click keeps its identity; noon is the prediction boundary, midnight the later batch snapshot.
vol2:fig-time-travel.question: Which clicks were available to the noon prediction?

vol2:fig-tinytl-architecture.name: original-v2-tinytl-architecture
vol2:fig-tinytl-architecture.scope: The original three-block comparison. Saved input tiles are schematic, not a memory-byte model. TinyTL freezes backbone weights and trains biases, lite residuals, and the classifier. Mask and normalization state may be retained or recomputed.
vol2:fig-tinytl-architecture.question: Why does a frozen backbone still need a backward pass?

vol2:fig-traditional-vs-ml-fleet.name: original-v2-traditional-vs-ml-fleet
vol2:fig-traditional-vs-ml-fleet.scope: Separate original map-task and synchronous-training examples; retained outputs and barrier dependencies.
vol2:fig-traditional-vs-ml-fleet.question: Why can one task retry alone while a shared update waits?

vol2:fig-ulysses-ownership-transpose.name: original-v2-ulysses-ownership-transpose
vol2:fig-ulysses-ownership-transpose.scope: Original four tokens × four heads × four ranks; head dimension omitted. Ordinary multihead attention with compatible divisibility; no GQA replication. Every token–head pair appears exactly once.
vol2:fig-ulysses-ownership-transpose.question: What changes ownership in Ulysses AllToAll?

vol3:fig-vol3-asynchronous-freshness-pip.name: original-v3-vol3-asynchronous-freshness-pipeline
vol3:fig-vol3-asynchronous-freshness-pip.scope: Original panels retained: synchronous four-member reference, asynchronous behavior versions, and one-record admission path. A and C sampled at v0, B at v1; A is checked at v1, B at v3, and C at v4. Declared maximum lag = 2 updates. This is a per-record check, not complete group eligibility.
vol3:fig-vol3-asynchronous-freshness-pip.question: Which record is still fresh at admission?

vol3:fig-vol3-chunked-timeline.name: original-v3-vol3-chunked-timeline
vol3:fig-vol3-chunked-timeline.scope: Original monolithic and chunked schedules retain their brackets, output-token markers, and canonical weight-only millisecond axes. Replay executes the monolithic schedule first, then eight mixed iterations. Playback time is illustrative, not the axis clock.
vol3:fig-vol3-chunked-timeline.question: How does chunking let existing decodes advance?

vol3:fig-vol3-first-token-accounting.name: original-v3-vol3-first-token-accounting
vol3:fig-vol3-first-token-accounting.scope: Original service/client split with illustrative output identities A, B, C (K = 3). Distances and playback durations are schematic.
vol3:fig-vol3-first-token-accounting.question: When does the first token become visible?

vol3:fig-vol3-index-invalidation.name: original-v3-vol3-index-invalidation
vol3:fig-vol3-index-invalidation.scope: The original three strategies are compared for one file. r17 → r18 → r19 are source generations, not elapsed-time units; costs are deliberately not resimulated.
vol3:fig-vol3-index-invalidation.question: Can a stale worker publish after a newer edit?

vol3:fig-vol3-overlapping-trace-interval.name: original-v3-vol3-overlapping-trace-intervals
vol3:fig-vol3-overlapping-trace-interval.scope: The original hypothetical one-host-clock intervals are retained. A second panel follows an independent operation with a late outcome; no benchmark or causal speedup is claimed.
vol3:fig-vol3-overlapping-trace-interval.question: Why is elapsed time smaller than the sum of work?

vol3:fig-vol3-sandbox-pool-lifecycle.name: original-v3-vol3-sandbox-pool-lifecycle
vol3:fig-vol3-sandbox-pool-lifecycle.scope: One instance, lease L1, and explicitly covered reset obligations. This is a success path; any failed or incomplete obligation requires removal from service.
vol3:fig-vol3-sandbox-pool-lifecycle.question: What permits a used sandbox to return to standby?

vol3:fig-vol3-tail-sampling-pipeline.name: original-v3-vol3-tail-sampling-pipeline
vol3:fig-vol3-tail-sampling-pipeline.scope: Toy trials A and B illustrate the original capture → bounded buffer → selector path and separate accounting path. Trial identity is preserved; no population-rate estimate is inferred.
vol3:fig-vol3-tail-sampling-pipeline.question: What survives when a diagnostic body is evicted?

vol1:fig-block-sparse-gemm.name: original-v1-block-sparse-gemm
vol1:fig-block-sparse-gemm.scope: Source pattern: a 3 × 3 grid of tiles, each dense tile 3 × 3; six stored tiles at (0,0),(0,1),(1,0),(1,2),(2,1),(2,2). Supporting numeric case: every stored scalar weight is 1; the activation column contains 1–9. Colors in the original do not encode these toy values.
vol1:fig-block-sparse-gemm.question: How do block coordinates select reads and retain output sums?

vol1:fig-ml-ops-dlrm-node-day.name: original-v1-ml-ops-dlrm-node-day
vol1:fig-ml-ops-dlrm-node-day.scope: Chapter scenario: eight H100 accelerators; serving and hot standby each occupy two, retraining occupies four for six hours. The source schedule runs retraining first, then admits a two-accelerator canary. These are occupancy commitments, not transfers of model bytes or a live cluster controller.
vol1:fig-ml-ops-dlrm-node-day.question: Can a canary fit without evicting the rollback copy?

vol1:fig-training-step-memory.name: original-v1-training-step-memory
vol1:fig-training-step-memory.scope: Source network 784–128–64–10, FP32, batch 32 and 1,024. Weights and two Adam buffers persist. Backward releases saved outputs as gradients accumulate. Meters share one scale across both batch cases; update leaves parameter-related state resident, including gradients. Clearing gradients is separate.
vol1:fig-training-step-memory.question: Why does batch size change the memory peak?

vol1:fig-depthwise-pointwise-channels.name: original-v1-depthwise-pointwise-channels
vol1:fig-depthwise-pointwise-channels.scope: The source has three input channels and two outputs at one spatial position, with depth multiplier one. Declared toy values: each 3 × 3 patch is constant 1, 2, or 3. Standard filters use weights 1 and 2. Depthwise weights are 1; pointwise rows are [1,1,1] and [1,0,−1]. Same shape does not imply equivalent layers.
vol1:fig-depthwise-pointwise-channels.question: Which spatial results can both output channels reuse?

vol1:fig-serving-chunked-prefill.name: original-v1-serving-chunked-prefill
vol1:fig-serving-chunked-prefill.scope: The source compares alternative schedules on one worker: the same prompt P has four work chunks; one active decode stream shares that worker. Slots are schematic ordered operations, not seconds. Decode creates one output token only after its operation completes. Both schedules begin with token 0 already emitted.
vol1:fig-serving-chunked-prefill.question: When can the active stream emit another token?
